Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# site-stats — what the worker does

Recounts the four canon-wide figures `site/data/promoted.js` promotes — packs,
deterministic checks, skills, scheduled task types — and lands the difference.

There is no `task.md` because there is no agent: counting is arithmetic over the
canon's own files, and [`task.mjs`](task.mjs) says why that makes the whole run code.

## The count

The site declares which canon it is about (`canonRepo`), so the worker follows that
rather than carrying the address a second time. It shallow-clones what it names and
reads the tree:

| Figure | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| packs | the rows of `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` |
| checks | per pack, its `README.md` rows whose enforcement cell reads `check:` |
| skills | per pack, the directory entries under `skills/` |
| tasks | per pack, the directory entries under `tasks/` |

Two properties of that table are the whole reason the counting is its own tested
module ([`count-canon-stats.mjs`](count-canon-stats.mjs)) rather than a few lines
inline:

- **The directory is the pack set, not `packs/`.** A pack absent from the directory
  is absent deliberately — the canary pack declares `hidden: true` so nothing offers
  it — so counting the checkout's directories counts a pack no one can adopt.
- **A check is a table *row*, never a heading.** The section is "Checks" in most
  packs, "The check" in `barriers`; the columns are `Check | Severity` in most,
  `Rule | Confidence` in `claudinite-tasks`; and `claudinite-lifecycle` puts two
  check tables under one heading. Anything that keys off the heading or the header
  cells silently undercounts all three. Counting check *files* is no better: checks
  ship as `declared-checks.json` entries, as `*Rules/*.mjs` modules and as modules
  bundled inside a skill, so any one glob is wrong in both directions.

Nine packs are prose-only and legitimately have no README and no `skills/` or
`tasks/` directory; they count zero rather than failing.

## The write

[`promoted-stats.mjs`](promoted-stats.mjs) substitutes each number into the entry
carrying its label, leaving the rest of the file — the spotlight above all — exactly
as it was. The page is hand-edited by promo runs, so it is rewritten in place and
never regenerated.

Two consequences worth knowing:

- **A run that recounts the same four numbers delivers nothing.** The comparison is
  against the base branch's copy, not the working tree, so it holds no matter what
  the checkout is sitting on.
- **A label that is gone parks the item for a decision** rather than being appended
  back. The entry is missing because a person rewrote the stats block, and a task
  that restores its own row is overruling that edit instead of maintaining it.

input.title: site-stats: task.mjs carries a constant, so it is the fleet's only local task declaration that is not pure data
input.body:
An audit of every `task.mjs` under a local pack across the fleet (6 files, in Shepherd, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator and here) found five that are a bare `export default { … }` object literal and one that is not: `site-stats`.

It declares a module constant and interpolates it:

```js
const PROMOTED_DIR = 'site/data';
…
automerge: [`under:${PROMOTED_DIR}`],
```

The file's own header already claims the stronger property — *"Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export."* — and the constant is used exactly once. Nothing about the declaration needs to be computed.

## Why it is worth flattening

A task declaration that is data can be read, diffed and validated without evaluating it. One template literal in one file is not a problem on its own; it is the single exception that stops "a local task declaration is a data object" from being true of the fleet.

## The part that needs care

`PROMOTED_DIR` is not shared with anything — `worker.mjs` declares its own `PROMOTED_PATH = 'site/data/promoted.js'` independently. So the two already drift freely, and the constant here guards nothing across the file boundary; it only names the value for the comment beside it.

Inlining cannot make that tie a real reference, because the point of the change is that `task.mjs` imports nothing. That is the case the basics rule covers — a value referred to from more than one place that genuinely cannot be shared needs a drift guard — so the flattening should land with one, in the `task.test.mjs` that already validates this declaration: the `under:` scope must contain the path the worker actually writes.

Without that, a future rename of `PROMOTED_PATH` leaves the automerge scope silently pointing at a folder the worker no longer writes to, and every recount parks for review with nothing to say why.

input.body:
Closes #418

`site-stats/task.mjs` was the one local task declaration in the fleet that was not a bare object literal. It declared a module constant and interpolated it into its single `automerge` term:

```js
const PROMOTED_DIR = 'site/data';
…
automerge: [`under:${PROMOTED_DIR}`],
```

The declaration now evaluates to the same policy from a literal, so the file matches its own header's claim — *"Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export."*

## Why it needed more than an inline

`PROMOTED_DIR` was never shared. `worker.mjs` declares `PROMOTED_PATH = 'site/data/promoted.js'` independently, so the two copies already drifted freely and the constant guarded nothing across the file boundary — it only named the value for the comment beside it.

The tie can't become a real reference, because the declaration importing nothing is the property being restored. That is the case the basics rule covers, so the copy gets a drift guard: `PROMOTED_PATH` is exported and `task.test.mjs` — which already validates this declaration — asserts the `under:` scope still contains the file the worker actually writes.

The failure it catches is silent in the worst direction. A rename of `PROMOTED_PATH` would leave the automerge scope pointing at a folder the worker no longer writes to, and every weekly recount would park for review with nothing saying why.

## Verification

The guard was written first and watched fail before it was made load-bearing — pointing the scope at `site/dataz` produces:

```

  error: 'automerge scopes ["site/dataz"] do not contain site/data/promoted.js'
```

- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 1 advisory (the pre-existing `file-placement` reach in `worker.mjs`, which that file's own comment records as deliberate)

No behaviour changes: the policy string, the counting and the delivery are identical.
